runs.detail: reading the ticket and the diff

brief.problem: When a customer's endpoint is down, a webhook delivery fails once and is never tried again. The customer finds out only when their own records drift. The ticket asks for deliveries to be retried for up to 24 hours and for the customer to see which ones failed.
brief.diagram:
flowchart LR A[Event happens
Delivery is sent inline] --> B[Endpoint is down
Error is logged, nothing stored] B --> C[Delivery is lost
No retry, no record, no notice]

options.title: Retry inside the request
options.argument_against: Holds the user's request open; cannot span 24 hours.

verdicts.why: A retry inside the request covers a blip and nothing longer.

options.title: Queue with backoff
options.argument_for: Meets the 24-hour window; failures are stored and visible.
options.argument_against: Needs an idempotency key so a retry is not a duplicate.

verdicts.why: Backoff runs to the 24 hours the ticket asks for.
The row per attempt is the record.

options.title: Dead-letter and manual replay
options.argument_for: A person can replay one delivery after fixing an endpoint.

verdicts.why: Nothing happens until a person replays it.
A dead-letter row is a record of the attempt.

brief.approach_verdict: B is the right shape for this ticket. It leaves out the one useful part of C: once the 24 hours run out there is no way to replay a delivery by hand. That is finding F2.
brief.provenance: from the ticket and the code · you corrected one sentence
brief.headline: Deliveries move to a queue, so one that fails is retried instead of lost.
brief.how_it_works_today: An event is delivered inside the request that caused it. The sender posts to the customer's endpoint, waits for the answer, and logs whatever came back. There is no record of a delivery anywhere apart from that log line, and nothing reads the log.
brief.flow_before_caption: The delivery is sent inside the request
brief.flow_after_caption: The delivery is queued, and a failure is kept

problems.label: The inline delivery
problems.was_wrong: A delivery that fails is never tried again.
problems.now_fixed: A worker retries it with backoff for 24 hours.
problems.detail_title: The delivery sent inside the request
detail_before: The sender posts to the endpoint and waits, inside the request that caused the event.
A timeout or a 500 is logged and the delivery is dropped.
The customer finds out when their own records drift.
detail_after: A delivery row is written before anything is sent.
A queue worker sends it and records what came back.
Backoff runs to 24 hours, after which the row stays failed.

problems.label: No record of an attempt
problems.was_wrong: Nothing records that a delivery was attempted.
problems.now_fixed: Every attempt is a row the customer can see.
detail_before: The only trace of a delivery is a log line nothing reads.
detail_after: One row per attempt, with its status and what came back.
The customer's own page lists the failed ones.

support_table.title: The idea: two questions, each with one owner

blind_pass.given: A web application delivers events to customer endpoints inside the request that caused them. A delivery that fails is logged and dropped. There is no record of an attempt anywhere else. Two things are wrong: a failed delivery is never tried again, and nothing records that a delivery was attempted.
blind_pass.pick_why: A queued delivery with its own row answers both problems at once, and the row is what the customer's page needs in any case.
questions: Is an endpoint allowed to receive the same delivery twice, or must a retry be idempotent?
How long after an event does a delivery stop being worth sending at all?

parts.title: The delivery row and its states
parts.summary: One row per attempt, written before anything is sent.

parts.title: The queue worker and its backoff
parts.summary: Sends a delivery, records the answer, and retries for 24 hours.

open_choices.left_open: How long a failed delivery is kept
open_choices.chosen: Thirty days, then the row is pruned
open_choices.why: The ticket asks for a 24-hour retry window and says nothing about the row afterwards.

disagreements.description_says: A retry carries the same idempotency key as the first attempt.
disagreements.code_does: The key is generated per attempt, so a retry is a new delivery to the endpoint.
